properties.name: Daum Lab — Living Systems Institute
properties.description:
**Bertram Daum** — University of Exeter, Exeter (GB)

ERC Starting Grant project engineering biohybrid microrobots by combining synthetic magnetic swimmers with S-layers -- highly stable, genetically-modifiable 2D protein arrays that form the cell walls of archaea and bacteria -- and the archaellum, a filamentous molecular rotary motor used by archaea for propulsion. The resulting biohybrid devices coat a magnetic swimmer with a dense, regularly-spaced affinity matrix for conjugating bioactive molecules at nanometre precision, targeting surgery, drug delivery, and nanotechnology applications.

**Why it's on this map:** Uses an actual living-organism-derived molecular structure (an archaeal cell-wall protein array and its associated rotary motor) as an engineered functional component of a synthetic device -- a concrete example of the biological-chassis approach to small-scale robotics, distinct from purely synthetic magnetic/acoustic actuation.

[[https://lsi.exeter.ac.uk/member/dr-bertram-daum/|Group website]]

Category: Biohybrid Robot · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: Tiantian Xu Group
properties.description:
**Tiantian Xu** — Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shenzhen (CN)

Professor at the Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Robotics and Intelligent System, leading extensive microrobot research: magnetic-acoustic sequentially actuated CAR-T cell microrobots for precision navigation and in-situ antitumor immunoactivation, untethered quadruped soft thin-film microrobots, and living microalgae-based magnetic microrobots for cancer therapy.

**Why it's on this map:** A prolific, diverse microrobotics research portfolio -- high-confidence direct fit, part of a real cluster of researchers at the same institute.

[[https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=jSv44msAAAAJ&hl=zh-CN|Group website]]

Category: Biohybrid Robot · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: Medical Microrobotics Lab
properties.description:
**Veronika Magdanz** — University of Waterloo, Waterloo, ON (CA)

Develops biohybrid and bioinspired microrobots for localized medical interventions, including sperm-based microrobots (IRONSperm: deactivated bovine sperm coated with magnetic nanoparticles, serving as a flexible drug-carrying template steered by external magnetic fields), sperm-nanoparticle interaction studies, and flexible microrobots for removing obstructions. PhD from TU Dresden (2016) on sperm-driven microrobots, Assistant Professor at Waterloo since 2022.

**Why it's on this map:** Works on externally magnetically-actuated micro/nanomotors -- a materials/actuation-technique match, part of the same broader regional research community as other magnetic-microrobot entries on this map.

[[https://magdanzlab.com/|Group website]]

Category: Biohybrid Robot · Smallest demonstrated: unknown
